text_blocks.snippet: Both ACE inhibitors and ARBs (angiotensin receptor blockers) are recognized as equal, first-line options for treating high blood pressure.
snippet_highlighted_words: Both ACE inhibitors and ARBs (angiotensin receptor blockers) are recognized as equal, first-line options for treating high blood pressure

list.snippet: Effectiveness: Both classes lower blood pressure and protect the heart and kidneys equally well.
Side Effects: ARBs are generally better tolerated and cause significantly fewer side effects than ACE inhibitors.
Historical Track Record: ACE inhibitors (such as lisinopril or enalapril) have a longer history and more legacy trial data, while ARBs (such as losartan or valsartan) became popular later.

list.snippet: Many modern reviews and large-scale studies suggest starting with an ARB over an ACE inhibitor primarily due to better patient comfort and adherence (fewer people stopping the drug due to a cough) .
If a patient starts on an ACE inhibitor and develops a chronic cough or swelling, doctors frequently switch them directly to an ARB.
